tool_args.rationale: The short-window gains are positive and consistent with the dual-horizon adaptation candidate, but they do not distinguish its long-timescale behavior. Since the forecast horizon is 19.9, a slow-horizon discriminating measurement is needed to identify and test the predicted endogenous reversal before fitting the final model.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the dual-horizon adaptation law from the five short-horizon rows
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The observations cover only H=0.16–0.48 and cannot identify the slow adaptation timescale or establish the predicted reversal near the target horizon H=19.9.
The cited candidate depends on x_now, which is zero in every supplied row, so these observations do not identify its oscillatory response.
An additional fine short-window trajectory is less discriminating for the long-horizon sign reversal than the targeted slow-horizon probe.
It is unrelated to the stated identifiability gap and has higher cost than useful alternatives.
